$comment: +++===+++ 2026-10-15 — Hasan Alizada — HAAL-165. Authorization policy for planning data (ADR-0005 sections 6–7): access is resolved per container from ownership and an active share; default deny; the admin role grants nothing on content. Used by every content endpoint and the sync API (server) and to hide unavailable actions (web app). PostgreSQL row-level security enforces the same rules as a second layer.
purpose: Decides whether a user may perform an action on a container (calendar, board, note) or its items, and which HTTP status a refusal maps to.

action.description: read: see the container and its items; write_items: create, update, move, soft-delete, restore items; manage_container: rename, archive, soft-delete the container; share: grant or revoke shares.

share_permission.description: Active (non-revoked) share of the container for the actor, if any.

deny_status.description: null when allowed; 404 when the actor may not even read (no existence leak); 403 when the actor can read but not perform the action.

invariants: the owner may perform every action (reason owner)
an edit share allows read and write_items (reason shared_edit); manage_container and share are refused with 403 (reason owner_only)
a view share allows read (reason shared_view); write_items is refused with 403 (reason view_only); manage_container and share with 403 (reason owner_only)
without ownership or an active share every action is refused with 404 (reason not_shared)
ownership wins over a share of the same actor
the actor role never changes the decision: administrators have no access to other users' content
allowed is true exactly when deny_status is null
